answer: Each agent identity lives in one $45 TPM chip whose key never leaves silicon, and the registry demands a fresh quote every epoch. Enrollment runs through a vine of manufacturer certificates quote checkers verify. Each epoch the chip signs the new seed with its counter, so a replayed quote is a relic and fails. A missed quote drops the identity to its nadir, zero weight and a burned slot. Forging 100 clones takes 100 chips at $45, $4,500, plus 20 minutes enrollment each, 33 hours, against $45 and 20 minutes for one honest agent. A copied key opens nothing when the lock keeps the secret.
